messages.subject: Re: [TMB users] Error in ev(obj$env$par) : Wrong range component.
parts:
Hey Gary, 

you are initializing your  normdens at 0 when you should be initializing it at 1.0. Otherwise everything else will turn to 0...

Also,  I'm not sure if TMB has element-wise multiplication.  Maybe someone else in the group can answer that?
I believe that  rowx*beta is equal to number, not a vector. So you might want to loop over T again for that. Here is a version of your code that worked for me:


#include <TMB.hpp>                
#include <Eigen/Dense>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() () {
  // Data
  DATA_MATRIX(x); 
  DATA_VECTOR(y);
  DATA_INTEGER(T);
  // Parameters
  PARAMETER(bi); 
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(beta);
  PARAMETER(sigma1); 
  PARAMETER(sigma2);
  
  Type mu = 0.0;
  Type murand = 0.0;
 
  vector<Type> rowx(T);
  vector<Type> tmp(T);
  
  Type normdens1=1.0;
  Type normdens2=1.0;
  Type prodclust=1.0;
  
 normdens2 = dnorm(bi,murand,sigma1,0);

 
  
  for (int j = 0; j < T; j++ ) {
    
    rowx = x.row(j);

    for (int i = 0; i < T; i++ ) {
      tmp(i) = rowx(i)*beta(i);
    }
    mu = sum(tmp)+bi;
    
    normdens1 *= dnorm(y(j),mu,sigma2,0);

    
   
  } 
  
  prodclust *= normdens1*normdens2;

  return prodclust;  

}


I hope this helps!


Catarina

Dear all TMB users

I'm doing joint distribution with TMB, but I met this error "Wrong range component." when I call nlminb(f$par,f$fn,f$gr).

//.cpp file
#include <TMB.hpp>                
#include <Eigen/Dense>

template<class Type>
Type objective_function<Type>::operator() () {
  // Data
  DATA_MATRIX(x); 
  DATA_VECTOR(y);
  DATA_INTEGER(T);
  // Parameters
  PARAMETER(bi); 
  PARAMETER_VECTOR(beta);
  PARAMETER(sigma1); 
  PARAMETER(sigma2);
  
  Type mu = 0.0;
  Type murand = 0.0;
 
  vector<Type> rowx(T);
  vector<Type> tmp(T);
  
  Type normdens1=0;
  Type normdens2=0;
  Type prodclust=0;
  
 normdens2 = dnorm(bi,murand,sigma1);
  
  for (int j = 0; j < T; j++ ) {
    
    rowx = x.row(j);
    tmp = rowx*beta;
    mu = sum(tmp)+bi;
    
    normdens1 *= dnorm(y(j),mu,sigma2);
   
  } 
  prodclust *= normdens1*normdens2;

  return prodclust;  
}

//R file

library(Rcpp)
library(TMB)                          
compile("test.cpp")             # Compile the C++ file
dyn.load(dynlib("test")) 
x<-rbind(c(1,1,0),c(1,0,1),c(1,0,0))
y <- as.vector(c(7.58,14.96,5.39))
T <- as.integer(3)
b.vec <- rep(rnorm(50,0,0.5),3)
Beta.vec <- matrix(c(5,2,10),ncol=1)
data <- list(x=x, y=y, T=T)
parameters <- list(bi=b.vec[1], beta =Beta.vec, sigma1=0.5,sigma2=0.7 )
f = MakeADFun(data,parameters,random = "bi",DLL="test")
#f$fn()
nlminb(f$par,f$fn,f$gr)



All suggestions on how to go about this problem are much appreciated.

Thanks,

gary

cwiseProduct() can be used for element wise multiplication. Alternatively,
you can use array types which use element wise operations by default.
See https://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/group__TutorialArrayClass.html for
